USMLE-style practice · Pharmacology

Anticoagulant choice during pregnancy

Choose the single best answer, then reveal the explanation.

A pregnant patient with acute venous thrombosis requires anticoagulation and does not have a mechanical heart valve. The team chooses a heparin-based regimen rather than routine warfarin treatment. Which difference is most relevant to fetal exposure?

  1. Heparin does not cross the placenta appreciably
  2. Warfarin is too large to cross the placenta
  3. Heparin accelerates fetal vitamin K production
  4. Warfarin protects fetal cartilage from injury
  5. Both agents have identical placental transfer
Reveal answer and explanation
Correct answer

Heparin does not cross the placenta appreciably

Heparins have negligible placental transfer; warfarin can harm the fetus.

Understanding the options

Heparin does not cross the placenta appreciably
Heparins have negligible placental transfer; warfarin can harm the fetus.
Warfarin is too large to cross the placenta
Warfarin crosses the placenta.
Heparin accelerates fetal vitamin K production
Fetal vitamin K production is not the protective mechanism.
Warfarin protects fetal cartilage from injury
Warfarin exposure can cause fetal abnormalities rather than protecting cartilage.
Both agents have identical placental transfer
Their placental transfer differs substantially.
